feedback: Decision: revise. This candidate is valid, but it drops the kd gain that produced the only progress gains so far. Iteration 1 (kd 0.30, sensors +/-0.04 m) raised s-bend progress from 0.040 to 0.157 and slalom from 0.035 to 0.110, which is the best raced score (52.35). Iteration 2 (kd 0.15, sensors +/-0.05 m) returned both tracks to baseline progress (0.040 and 0.035), so the candidate's kd of 0.15 is the likely reason those tracks are slow. Widening the sensors to +/-0.05 m reduced oval line-loss events from 1 to 0 but left oval progress at 0.115 and max_error at 0.0614, so it has not solved the oval. The base_speed change to 1.4 is a fair single test of the oval corner: the oval fails at a fixed progress point, and max_error sits just over the 0.06 m limit, which points to speed into the corner. Oscillation in iteration 1 (0.154 and 0.158) was only just above the 0.15 threshold, and that threshold is a guide, not a score term. Revise so the next race tests the speed change while restoring the kd that gave the best progress. Next steps depend on the race: if oval progress still stalls at 0.115 at base_speed 1.4, test a larger sensor_size (0.016) or a different line_loss search direction. If s-bend and slalom still show one line-loss event each, test line_loss = search_right or search_left, keeping the other fields fixed. Change one field group at a time so the cause of each effect stays clear.
requested_changes: Restore controller.kd to 0.30, keeping kp 4.0 and ki 0.05. Iteration 1 showed kd 0.30 gave the only s-bend and slalom progress gains (0.157 and 0.110 against baseline 0.040 and 0.035), and iteration 2 showed kd 0.15 lost them.
Keep controller.base_speed at 1.4, as tested in this candidate, to check whether slower entry lets the oval hold the line (oval max_error was 0.0614 at base_speed 1.6 with progress 0.115 unchanged).

If line_loss_events stays at 1 on s-bend or slalom after this change, set controller.line_loss to search_right or search_left. Iterations 0 to 2 show last_direction gave one line-loss event per run on those tracks.
